scenarios.criterion: implementation.schema.json and qa.schema.json each gain an optional filesDeleted or testFilesDeleted array of paths, generated from the Go structs (never hand-edited), with a description stating that a rename is the new path in filesCreated and the old path in filesDeleted.
scenarios.name: Generated schemas document the new deletion fields and the rename convention
given: the ImplementationState and QAState Go structs declare filesDeleted and testFilesDeleted fields
then: implementation.schema.json contains an optional filesDeleted array of paths
qa.schema.json contains an optional testFilesDeleted array of paths
each field's description states that a rename is encoded as the new path in filesCreated and the old path in filesDeleted

scenarios.criterion: A stage that lists a path in filesDeleted passes the claim when the path is absent now and existed when the stage started, observed as the path appearing in the posture check's changed-paths set (which reports status against the run's base commit).
scenarios.name: A deletion claim passes when the path is gone now and was present at stage start
given: a stage lists a path in filesDeleted
the path existed when the stage started and is absent from disk now
the posture check's changed-paths set, measured against the run's base commit, includes that path
when: the filesDeleted claim is checked for that stage

scenarios.criterion: A path in filesDeleted that still exists on disk fails the stage with a ClaimError naming the field and the path: "the file still exists — the stage reported a deletion it did not do".
scenarios.name: A deletion claim fails when the file still exists on disk
given: a stage lists a path in filesDeleted
the path still exists on disk
when: the filesDeleted claim is checked for that stage
then: the stage fails with a ClaimError naming the field and the path
the error message reads "the file still exists — the stage reported a deletion it did not do"

scenarios.criterion: A path in filesDeleted that never existed (absent now and absent from the posture check's changed-paths set) fails the stage with a ClaimError: "no such file was there to delete".
scenarios.name: A deletion claim fails when the path never existed
given: a stage lists a path in filesDeleted
the path is absent from disk now
the path is absent from the posture check's changed-paths set
when: the filesDeleted claim is checked for that stage
then: the stage fails with a ClaimError reading "no such file was there to delete"

scenarios.criterion: An entry containing " -> " in any path-naming field (filesCreated, filesModified, filesDeleted, testFilesCreated, testFilesModified, testFilesDeleted, or security's filesModified) fails validation with a message instructing the caller to list the new path in filesCreated and the old path in filesDeleted.
scenarios.name: A rename encoded as an arrow in a path field is rejected before claim-checking
given: a stage's state document lists an entry containing " -> " in a path-naming field
then: validation fails before any claim is checked
the error message instructs the caller to list the new path in filesCreated and the old path in filesDeleted

scenarios.criterion: requireTouchedFiles counts an implementation that only deletes files as having touched something; it no longer requires filesCreated or filesModified to be non-empty when filesDeleted names at least one path.
scenarios.name: A deletion-only implementation satisfies the touched-files requirement
given: an implementation state document with empty filesCreated and empty filesModified
the same document names at least one path in filesDeleted
then: the document is accepted as having touched something
requireTouchedFiles does not demand a non-empty filesCreated or filesModified

scenarios.criterion: An existing state document with no filesDeleted or testFilesDeleted field (the omitempty default) validates exactly as it did before this change — no new required field, no changed behavior for filesCreated/filesModified/testFilesCreated/testFilesModified claims.
scenarios.name: A state document without a deleted-files field validates unchanged
given: a state document with no filesDeleted field and no testFilesDeleted field
when: the document is validated and its claims are checked
then: validation succeeds with no new required field
the existing filesCreated, filesModified, testFilesCreated, and testFilesModified claims behave exactly as before this change

scenarios.criterion: Every new or changed function has cyclomatic complexity below 7 (enforced by golangci-lint's gocyclo, already configured at min-complexity 7 in .golangci.yml), every changed line is covered by a test proven able to fail, go test ./... and the lint pass, and no file outside scope.paths (internal/state/**, internal/orchestrator/**, shared/schemas/pipeline/**, docs/features/state-files-deleted/**) changes.
scenarios.name: The implementation meets the project's complexity, coverage, and scope bars
given: the filesDeleted feature has been implemented
when: the set of changed files is compared against scope.paths
then: every new or changed function has cyclomatic complexity below 7
every changed line is covered by a test that fails when that line is reverted
go test ./... and the lint pass both succeed
no changed file falls outside internal/state/**, internal/orchestrator/**, shared/schemas/pipeline/**, or docs/features/state-files-deleted/**
